content: It may also be prescribed for other conditions as determined by your healthcare provider. Hydralazine is available in several forms, including oral tablets (10 mg, 25 mg, 50 mg, and 100 mg) and injectable forms. Always store it in a cool, dry place, and keep the container tightly closed. Before starting hydralazine, inform your healthcare provider about all your current and past health conditions, including heart disease (such as coronary artery disease or a history of heart attack), kidney disease, stroke, or rheumatic fever. Additionally, disclose any prescription or over-the-counter medications, vitamins, minerals, herbal products, or other supplements you are taking, as hydralazine may interact with these substances. If you are pregnant, planning to become pregnant, or breastfeeding, let your healthcare provider know. It is not fully understood how hydralazine may affect pregnancy or an unborn baby, but it does pass into breast milk. Your provider will advise you on whether it is safe to use hydralazine in these situations. Hydralazine does not have known interactions with food or nonalcoholic drinks. However, it is unclear if alcohol consumption affects hydralazine. Drinking alcohol while taking this medication may increase the risk of dizziness. If you miss a dose of hydralazine, take it as soon as you remember. If it is almost time for your next dose, skip the missed dose and take only the next scheduled dose. Do not take double or extra doses. In the event of an overdose, seek immediate medical attention by calling 911 or contacting a Poison Control Center at 800-222-1222. Common side effects of hydralazine include headache, decreased appetite, nausea, vomiting, diarrhea, a pounding or fast heartbeat, and chest pain or discomfort. If any of these side effects bother you, inform your healthcare provider. Serious side effects, though less common, include lupus-like symptoms (rash, joint pain, fever, weakness, swollen glands, reduced urination, or discolored urine), chest pain (which may indicate a heart attack), blood disorders (such as agranulocytosis, anemia, or low white blood cell count), and nerve problems (peripheral neuropathy). If you experience any of these symptoms, contact your healthcare provider immediately. Hydralazine should not be used by individuals allergic to its ingredients, those with coronary artery disease (as it may increase the risk of heart attack), or those with mitral valvular rheumatic heart disease (as it may strain the heart). Always take hydralazine as prescribed by your healthcare provider and do not share it with others, even if they have similar conditions. Keep this medication out of reach of children. Hydralazine may affect your alertness or coordination. Avoid driving or engaging in activities requiring full alertness until you know how the medication affects you. Always consult your healthcare provider for guidance specific to your health and medication needs.
